5436.idn: Name in the source: Sangkong (Sangkong 桑孔); family in the source: Southern Loloish, Lolo-Burmese (similar to Hani and Bisu); Tibeto-Burman

tn.quote: Syllable structure is CV(C), and each syllable is pronounced with a distinctive lexical tone. … Sangkong preserves the three Proto-Lolo-Burmese [PLB] tonal categories A, B, C intact in unchecked syllables. … Phonemically, the DL and DS tones may be considered, by virtue of tone contour and complementary distribution, to be allotones of C and B respectively. In addition to these tones, a high rising tone is found in loan words and sandhi environments. … Tones (p. 54) 55 A high level 31 B [42] DS low falling 33 C [44] DL mid level 35 high rising
tn.cite: Handel, Zev. 2004. Review of Li Yongsui, A study of Sangkong [Sangkongyu yanjiu] (Beijing 2002, 403 pp.). Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 27(1): 111-142. DOI 10.32655/LTBA.27.1.05.

tn.note: Every syllable carries a lexical tone: high level 55, low falling 31, mid level 33, plus high rising 35 in loans, sandhi and contracted syllables; checked syllables take 42/44 as allotones of 31/33. tn.quote: There are three tones in the Phaipha dialect: high (i.e. /tsʰɘ́/ ‘blood’), mid (i.e. /tsʰɘ/ ‘wind’), and low (i.e. /tsʰɘ̀ / ‘slide’). 5438.idn: Name in the source: 松林語 (Songlin; Japanese reading ソンリン; self-designation of the village sɑŋ31 lin55); family in the source: Tibeto-Burman; an independent language, not Tibetic; the book assigns it to 藏語支 (Bodish), which the reviewer finds unproven

tn.quote: • 音節声調で、３つの対立がある 本書の分析では、音節ごとに声調を認め、55、24、31 の３種が対立することになっている。注意すべきは複音節語の構成要素になったとき変調することがあるという指摘（p. 24）で、変化しないか 33 か 31 と記述する。 … 本書では 42 という声調が疑問詞、疑問文、願望文で現れると指摘する（p. 24）。特定の文の形式に現れることから、語に備わった声調ではなくイントネーションなど韻律的特徴と判断でき … 本書では声調に文法的機能があると述べ（p. 25）、31 調が主に機能語に現れるという観察を提示している。一方で格標識は 55 調で固定されている
tn.translation: • Syllable tone, three contrasts. In the book's analysis a tone is recognised on every syllable and three kinds, 55, 24 and 31, contrast. Noteworthy is the remark (p. 24) that a syllable may change tone inside a polysyllabic word: unchanged, 33, or 31. … The book notes that a tone 42 appears on interrogatives, in questions and optatives (p. 24). As it occurs in particular sentence types it can be judged prosodic (intonation), not a tone of the word … The book states that tone has a grammatical function (p. 25), tone 31 appearing mainly on function words, while case markers are fixed at tone 55
tn.cite: 鈴木博之 (Suzuki, Hiroyuki). 2023. [書評] 宋成、謝穎瑩、李大勤、李佐文（著）《西藏察隅松林語》北京：商務印書館、2019 年、10+272pp. 言語記述論集 (Journal of Kijutsuken, Descriptive Linguistics Study Group) 15: 75-84. 言語記述研究会.

tn.quote: Tone carries an important function in the language, both lexically and grammatically. There are two level tones. In this paper, high tone is marked by acute accent and low tone unmarked but considered. The falling tone is marked by circumflex on the vowel. Rising tone is indicated by using two vowels with a low high pattern. … The suffix -i attaches to nominative singular nouns and the suffixes -a, -na attach to nominative plural nouns. A tone change from the tone of the accusative noun can mark both nominative singular and plural nouns.

5444.idn: Name in the source: Totela (K41); Zambian Totela (ZT) vs Namibian Totela (NT, K411); family in the source: Bantu, Bantu Botatwe (BB) group (K30–40 and M60 groups); ZT resembles Group M Tonga and Ila

tn.quote: Totela’s tone system can be analysed as H/Ø. An alternative analysis, proposed by Hyman (2007 for Tonga; 2016 for Totela) is a L vs. Ø system. Surface (non-intonational) tones can be H or L on short vowels, and H:, L: or HL falling on long vowels. … Nouns can have underlying H tone on any stem syllable, although surface HH is prohibited. Verbs have a lexical contrast between root H and Ø. … The most striking feature of the Totela tone system is High-tone anticipation (HTA), in which an underlying H tone surfaces on the preceding syllable.
tn.cite: Crane, Thera. 2019. Totela K41. In Mark Van de Velde, Koen Bostoen, Derek Nurse & Gérard Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 2nd edn (Routledge Language Family Series), 645-691. London–New York: Routledge. doi:10.4324/9781315755946 (HELDA electronic reprint, hdl 10138/309934)

tn.note: Privative H vs toneless (surface H and L; HL fall on long vowels); nouns may bear H on any stem syllable, verb roots H vs Ø; H surfaces one syllable early (anticipation); downstep; downdrift. Checked against the source (tone consistency check round 3, 2026-09-24): floating unstated -> yes (sec. 2.3 reprint p. 7; sec. 4.2.10 reprint p. 36).

corr.words: TAMN forms have three main melodic tone patterns … If an input final H (including grammatical Hs) meets an input initial H … Totela verbs take three main tone patterns: 1. Underlying tones surface (with high tone anticipation) without any melodic tones … 2. Melodic H on second root syllable … 3. Melodic H on final syllable, surfacing on the penultimate syllable

5445.idn: Name in the source: Tuki (Kombe dialect); family in the source: Bantu (classified as A.64 by Guthrie 1967-1971)

tn.quote: On the surface, Tuki has H, L and (downstepped) !H tone. While HL falling tones do occur, LH rising tones are much rarer and appear never to occur on a single mora. As we shall discuss below, only vowels (henceforth “moras”) can carry tone in Tuki. Since there is a vowel length contrast in Tuki, CVV syllables count as two moras, while CV syllables count as one. … we Tecognize an underlying L vs. H opposition on verb roots … while the Kombe dialect has a terrace-level system with downstepped H tones, the Bacenga dialect described by Hyman (1980) has a discrete level tone system with H, M and L.
tn.cite: Hyman, Larry M. & Edmond Biloa. 1992. Transparent Low Tone in Tuki. Proceedings of the Eighteenth Annual Meeting of the Berkeley Linguistics Society: Special Session on the Typology of Tone Languages, 104-127. doi:10.3765/bls.v18i2.1547

tn.note: Kombe dialect: two underlying tones, H vs L, carried by moras; H spreads rightward; downstepped H after a delinked or floating L (terraced levels). Bacenga dialect reported with discrete H, M, L.

5446.idn: Name in the source: cʋ́ràmã̀ (langue des Turka; also cited as Turka, Tourouka, tyurama); family in the source: groupe Gur de la famille Niger-Congo (Heine et Nurse 2004); Proto-central, Sud, next to kirma

tn.quote: Une observation au niveau des tons des items où il est attesté une palatalisation permet de confirmer que ce phénomène est effectivement la réalisation d’un phonème vocalique /I/. Le cʋ́ràmã̀ est une langue à ton, avec deux tonèmes que sont le ton haut (H) et le ton bas (B) selon M. Beogo (2021) Les exemples ci-dessous sont une preuve de cette pertinence du ton en cʋ́ràmã̀ . (5) bá « rester » bà « ils » pá « acheter, payer » pã̀ « généreux » … ce ton quitte son segment et s’associe au ton suivant qui est réalisé désormais modulé (montant ou descendant).
tn.translation: An observation of the tones of the items in which palatalisation is attested confirms that this phenomenon is indeed the realisation of a vowel phoneme /I/. Cʋrama is a tone language, with two tonemes, namely the high tone (H) and the low tone (B), following M. Beogo (2021). The examples below are proof of this distinctiveness of tone in Cʋrama. (5) bá 'stay' bà 'they' pá 'buy, pay' pã̀ 'generous' … this tone leaves its segment and associates with the following tone, which is then realised as a contour (rising or falling).
tn.cite: Beogo, Madou. 2024. Statut de la palatalisation en cʋ́ràmã̀ / Status of palatalization in cʋ́ràmã̀. Contextes Didactiques, Linguistiques et Culturels (CDLC) 2(2): 240-254. E-ISSN 2992-0515. Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo, Ouagadougou.
tn.locator: pp. 251-252, section 2.2 'Analyses des données' (tone behaviour under palatalisation, examples (5)-(7)); method p. 246
tn.note: Two level tones, high and low, contrastive (bá 'stay' vs bà 'they'); when a front vowel becomes [j] its tone re-links to the next vowel, giving a rising or falling contour.

tn.quote: Vaiphei is a tonal language like other related Tibeto-Burman languages. … This analysis proposes that Vaiphei has three contrastive tones, two contour tones (rising and falling) and a low tone. … In the study, the Chao tone number system (used in the International Phonetic Alphabet) is used to transcribe phonetic surface tones. Tone 1 Low 21 Tone 2 Rising 23 Tone 3 Falling 52 … In Vaiphei, all the three tones low, rising and falling occur on both open and closed syllables.
tn.cite: Suantak, Khawlsonkim. 2013. Vaiphei Phonetics, Phonology and Morphology: A Descriptive Study. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, School of Humanities, North-Eastern Hill University, Shillong. xi+284 pp. (Shodhganga hdl 10603/169680)

tn.note: Three contrastive tones on the syllable: low (21), rising (23) and falling (52); rising and falling do not occur before final glottal stop; low becomes rising after a rising tone in compounds.

5448.loc: p. 243, section 3 'La comparaison des deux systèmes consonantique et vocalique (wandala/fulfulde)'
5448.idn: Name in the source: wandala; family in the source: langue tchadique centrale (Central Chadic)

tn.quote: Du point de vue phonétique, principale différence entre les deux systèmes vocaliques: le fulfulde ne possède pas de voyelle centrale haute [ə]. Pour ce qui est du système consonantique, le fulfulde n’a pas de labio-vélaires (kw, gw, ngw) ni de latérales fricatives (ɬ, ɮ). Le wandala, quant à lui est dépourvu de nasale palatale (ny). Le fulfulde est une langue sans tons, alors que le wandala en registre deux tonals (haut et bas).
tn.translation: From the phonetic point of view, the main difference between the two vowel systems: Fulfulde has no high central vowel [ə]. As for the consonant system, Fulfulde has no labio-velars (kw, gw, ngw) nor lateral fricatives (ɬ, ɮ). Wandala, for its part, lacks the palatal nasal (ny). Fulfulde is a language without tones, whereas Wandala registers two tones [printed 'deux tonals'] (high and low).
tn.cite: Made Boukar. 2023. Le wandala – tchadique central – en contact avec le fulfulde au nord du Cameroun. Revue DELLA/Afrique (ACAREF), vol. 5, n° spécial – décembre 2023, Tome 1 (Lettres, langues, arts, éducation, enseignement, pédagogie, didactique), pp. 237-252.
tn.locator: p. 243, section 3 'La comparaison des deux systèmes consonantique et vocalique (wandala/fulfulde)'
tn.note: Two tones, high and low, stated in one sentence of a Wandala-Fulfulde contact study; no further tone description, though the borrowed forms listed are printed with tone accents.

tn.quote: In Wawa, ideophones are usually easily recognisable for their preference of rare phonemes (e.g. labial-velar stops), their preference of high (1) and low (4) tones and 1-4 and 4-1 contours (in a 4-level tone system), and for featuring consonants in positions not normally allowed in the phonology of other Wawa words. … Generally, in the Wawa lexicon, contour tones are very common and all combinations exist, except 1-3 and 3-1.

tn.quote: Tone in Syer and Supyire is marked on every vowel as follows: the acute accent is used to mark High tone, grave accent to mark Low tone. Absence of a tone on a vowel corresponds to Mid tone. Contour tones on short vowels are marked as a combination of register tones: a haček stands for a LH (ǎ), a circumflex for a HL (â), the grave accent + hyphen for Low-Mid (a᷅), and on long vowels by L on the first vowel and Ø on the second (àa). … The realization of the conditional in intransitive clauses for all three tonal classes of verbs is illustrated in (18).
tn.cite: Dombrowsky-Hahn, Klaudia. 2019. Conditional-relatives in Senufo (Gur) and Manding (Mande): The encoding of generalizing relative clauses in West African languages. 5451.loc: p. 120, Lautlehre Kap. I par. 1-2 'Tonhoehen' (par. 3 continues on p. 121)
5451.idn: Name in the source: /Xam-Buschmännisch (Dialekt der /xam-Buschmänner); family in the source: Buschmannsprachen (Bushman); in D. Bleek's quoted remark 'Südbuschmännisch' (Southern Bushman), contrasted with Nordbuschmännisch (!Kung)

tn.quote: § 1. Buschmännisch gehört zu den „Tonhöhensprachen“, d. h. Sprachen, welche sonst völlig gleiche Wörter in verschiedenen Bedeutungen durch verschiedene Tonhöhen bzw. -bewegungen unterscheiden. Über Tonhöhen im Buschm. erfahren wir aus unseren Texten wenig. … wozu D. Bl. brieflich folgendes bemerkt: „Südbuschmännisch, wie z. B. die /χam-Sprache, hat im Vergleich wenige hohe und tiefe Töne. …“ § 2. Nach D. Bleeks brieflichen Mitteilungen wäre allerdings für den Tiefton ein häufiges Zeichen in der Gestalt eines Hakens, unter dem Vokal gebraucht
tn.translation: Par. 1. Bushman belongs to the 'pitch (tone) languages', i.e. languages which distinguish otherwise wholly identical words of different meanings by different pitches or pitch movements. ... About pitches in Bushman we learn little from our texts. ... D. Bl[eek] remarks by letter as follows: 'Southern Bushman, e.g. the /Xam language, has comparatively few high and low tones. Northern Bushman, such as !Kung, has many more.' ... Par. 2. According to D. Bleek's communications by letter, however, a frequent sign for the low tone, in the shape of a hook under the vowel, is used
tn.cite: Meriggi, Piero. 1928/29. Versuch einer Grammatik des /Xam-Buschmännischen. Zeitschrift für Eingeborenen-Sprachen 19: 117-153, 188-205. Berlin: D. Reimer.
tn.locator: p. 120, Lautlehre Kap. I par. 1-2 'Tonhoehen' (par. 3 continues on p. 121)
tn.note: Called a tone language; texts mark a raised (high) tone and, per D. Bleek, a low tone (hook); /Xam said to have few high and low tones; grave/acute on some pronouns read as low/high; no count given. Checked against the source (tone consistency check, 2026-09-23): quotation re-keyed from the source (p. 120, Lautlehre Kap. I §§ 1-2 'Tonhöhen').

5452.idn: Name in the source: XZ Lalo (Xuzhang Lalo; also 'Xuzhang Lalu'); family in the source: Lalo < Central Ngwi < Ngwi (Loloish) < Burmic (Lolo-Burmese) < Tibeto-Burman (Bradley 2002b)

tn.quote: XZ Lalo shares the same syllable template as YL: (C)V(N)T, in which the optional initial is one of 30 consonants, an obligatory vowel (one of 13 vowels or 1 syllabic fricative), an optional nasal final /-,/, and tone (one of 4). All tones are in modal phonation. … Unlike any other Lalo variety, XZ has merged *3, *H, *L to the mid level tone [33]. The resulting system contrasts four tones: High, Mid, Low, and Low-rising, as seen in Table 3-46 below. … The Tone *1 split and merger of *3, *H and *L leaves XZ with three equally spaced level tones and one rising tone.
tn.cite: Yang, Cathryn. 2010. Lalo regional varieties: phylogeny, dialectometry, and sociolinguistics. PhD thesis, Linguistics Program, La Trobe University, Bundoora, Victoria. doi:10.26181/21844209.v1

tn.note: Four tones on every (C)V(N) syllable, all modal voice: high 55 (often [453] in isolation), mid 33, low 21 and low-rising 24; three level tones and one rising; F0 plots of one speaker.

5454.idn: Name in the source: Yintale (also Yintalaing, Yantalaing; Shan 'Yangtalai'; Kayah 'Tah-liah'); family in the source: Karen (Karenic) languages, Sino-Tibetan; 'a south-western group of Kayah' (Bradley 1997 cited)

tn.quote: According to this data, all tones are in contrast. There are five contrastive tones in Yintale. Each tone is referred to by demonstrating diacritics. They are high //, mid //, low //, falling // and rising //. … According to this data, there are five phonemic tones in Yintale: high, falling, mid, low and rising. … With five tones and three syllable words, the number of possible patterns is 125, but only twenty-six patterns are seen in this data. Rising and falling tones tend to occur only on the third syllable, sequences of HH-X and HM-X are common as are LH-X and LL-X.

refs.ref: Apia, N’Guessan Edmond. 2025. L’abbey: à l’épreuve d’un alphabet et d’une orthographe stables. Djiboul, Revue des Arts-Communication, Lettres, Sciences Humaines et Sociales, N°009, Vol. 3 (juillet 2025), pp. 240-251. Abidjan: Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny.

5456.idn: Name in the source: abbey; family in the source: langue kwa de Côte d’Ivoire (Kwa)

tn.quote: L’abbey est une langue à tons. On y rencontre deux types de tons lexicaux: les tons ponctuels et les tons modulés. Les tons ponctuels sont au nombre de trois; ce sont: les tons haut, moyen et bas, représentés, respectivement, par les symboles (ˊ), ( ̄ ) et (ˋ). … Quant au ton moyen, il ne se rencontre qu’en position médiane et en position finale. … Les tons modulés, quant à eux, sont au nombre de deux; ce sont: les tons modulés descendant et montant. … Tous les tons sont marqués au-dessus des noyaux de syllabes que sont les voyelles. Exemples: cá [cá] « Epoux »; jā [jā] « Epouse » …
tn.translation: Abbey is a tone language. Two types of lexical tones occur: level tones and contour tones. The level tones are three: high, mid and low, written (ˊ), (̄) and (ˋ). … The mid tone occurs only in medial and final position. … The contour tones are two: falling and rising. … All tones are marked above the syllable nuclei, i.e. the vowels. Examples: cá 'husband'; jā 'wife' …
tn.cite: Apia, N’Guessan Edmond. 2025. L’abbey: à l’épreuve d’un alphabet et d’une orthographe stables. Djiboul, Revue des Arts-Communication, Lettres, Sciences Humaines et Sociales, N°009, Vol. 3 (juillet 2025), pp. 240-251. Abidjan: Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny.
tn.note: Tone language with three level tones (high, mid, low) and two contour tones (falling, rising), marked on every syllable nucleus; mid tone never word-initial except in numerals; nothing on stress.

5456.cfw: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

tn.quote: The basic tone-bearing unit is the syllabic, syllables (with a few special exceptions) being of the pattern CV (consonant - vowel), V (vowel) or N (syllabic nasal). Each of these normally bears a single unit of tone, viz. high, mid or low (abbreviated H, M and L respectively). … When the tone associated with a non-word-initial V or N syllable differs from that of a preceding syllable (which must be of structure CV) the two tones together are realised as a rising or falling pitch extending over the two syllables …

tn.note: Three level tones, high, mid and low, one on each syllable (CV, V or syllabic nasal); rising and falling glides analysed as sequences of two level tones; verbs fall into H, M and L tone classes.

5461.idn: Name in the source: Bhele; family in the source: Bantu (Grammar page: noun class system 'typical of many Bantu languages', 'related Bantu languages')

tn.quote: Bhele has two tone registers, High and Low. All four pa erns of High and Low are a ested on disyllabic noun roots. Contour tones can be seen as a combina on of a Low and a High tone, linked to the same syllable. … Verb roots have either a High tone or a Low tone, linked to the ﬁrst syllable of the root. … Some disyllabic High nouns are realized with a High tone on the ﬁrst syllable and a lower tone (but not at the level Low) on the second. As yet it is unknown whether this is another tone level, or (non)automa c downstep. … Bhele has gramma cal tone …
tn.cite: Raymond, Timothy R. & Gerrit de Wit. 2025. Notes on Bhele phonology ('Phonology page', final v3, dated June 2025). In: Bhele Dictionary (Bhele - French - Swahili - English), Webonary.org. SIL Global.
tn.locator: section 'Tone' (pages unnumbered)
tn.note: Two level tones, High and Low, linked to syllables; contours are Low+High on one syllable; High downstepped to Mid after certain High prefixes; floating High object prefixes; TAM verb tone melodies. Checked against the source (tone consistency check, 2026-09-23): floating yes -> unstated.

corr.words: For the ﬁrst- and second-person plural object preﬁxes, the ﬂoa ng High tone links to the vowel of the preceding subject preﬁx. ... If the vowel of the subject preﬁx has a High tone (the third person plural bá-), the ﬂoa ng High tone simply merges with the preceding High tone.

5462.idn: Name in the source: Bishnupriya Manipuri; family in the source: Eastern form of Indo-Aryan language family; developed under Magadhi-Apabhramsa; sisterly relation with Assamese, Bengali and Oriya; distinct from Meitei (Tibeto-Burman)

tn.quote: 2. Typological features of Bishnupriya a) Like most of the non-tonal Indo-Aryan languages, Bishnupriya is a non-tonal language. b) The basic structure of syllable in Bishnupriya is CVC. c) Like other Indo-Aryan languages, Bishnupriya roots are generally monosyllabic in nature. d) Bishnupriya language follows the SOV word order.
